Get ready

Bench r1: build it one step at a time

105 steps. One small thing per page. Do the numbered moves, then tick the box in the corner.

In every drawing, the glowing part is what you add now. Faded parts are already done.

The coloured bar at the top shows how far along you are. Take a break at every "done" page. Stopping mid-phase is fine too: the tick boxes show where you left off.

+ rail and red wires: 3V3 or battery plus − rail: ground black wires: ground blue wire: SDA (I2C data) yellow wire: SCL (I2C clock) do this now

h24 means row h, column 24. Columns run 62 on the left down to 1 on the right.

GND ↓27 is a hole in the blue − (ground) rail along the bottom edge, straight below column 27. 3V3 ↓18 is the red + rail, bottom edge, below column 18. An ↑ arrow means the rails along the top edge.

Get ready

Before you start

Gather these.

  • 3 breadboards, the plate, standoffs, WAGO holders
  • BOJACK jumpers: 1 × 1-hole, 4 × 2-hole, 8 × 3-hole, 2 × 4-hole, 1 × 5-hole
  • Duponts: 1 × M-F, 10 cm, 4 × M-F, 20 cm, 2 × M-F, 30 cm, 4 × M-M, 10 cm, 9 × M-M, 20 cm
  • Resistors: 4 × 10k 1%, 1 × 1M 1%, 3 × 10k; capacitors: 3 × 100 nF, 1 × 220 uF; 2 × 2-pin headers
  • 20 AWG and 22 AWG wire, strippers, a small screwdriver, tape

Already done in prep (design.md section 3): headers soldered on every module, the #4755 THERM jumper cut, the USB-C leads soldered, the pigtails made.

Safety: the pack stays unplugged until the last page. Nothing that carries battery current goes into a breadboard.

Boardsstep 1 of 105

Lay out the three breadboards

You need3 × Elegoo 830-point breadboards
masking tape and a pen
  1. Put the three breadboards on the plate as drawn. Back edge at the top.
  2. Label them with tape: BB2 at the back, BB1 in the middle, BB3 at the front.
  3. Each board: printed 1 on the right, row a at the top.
Check itColumn 62 is on the left of every board.
Bench r1 build guide · generated from layout/build.py and routing.py · drawings are to scale; header positions on modules are estimates until measured
Prepstep 2 of 105

Tape the TX NUCLEO's 5 V pins

You needthe TX NUCLEO
Kapton tape and a fine pen
  1. Six NUCLEO pins carry 5 V. Nothing on this bench uses them, and one wire on them would put 5 V on the 3V3 parts.
  2. Cover each with a small square of Kapton, written NO 5V: CN6 pin 5, CN6 pin 8, CN7 pin 6, CN7 pin 18, CN7 pin 24, CN10 pin 8.
  3. The two on CN6 are sockets: tape over the hole. The four on CN7 and CN10 are pins: fold the tape over the pin.
Check itSix squares of tape, none on CN6 pin 4 (3V3) or CN7 pin 16 (3V3): those two are used.
TipCN7 pin 7 is BOOT0 and CN7 pin 14 is RESET: nothing goes on them either. A wire on either and the board stays silent.
Bench r1 build guide · generated from layout/build.py and routing.py · drawings are to scale; header positions on modules are estimates until measured
Prepstep 3 of 105

Give each INA228 its own address

You needthe four INA228 boards (#5832)
soldering iron, thin solder, flux
tape and a pen
  1. The four INA228s share one I2C bus, so each needs its own address. New, they are all 0x40.
  2. On the back, beside Addr: pad pairs A0 and A1. Solder across a pair ties that pin to power; open, it reads ground.
  3. The pair beside VBus (SJ1) joins VBUS to VIN+.
  4. Do all four now, before the breadboards.
Check itTurned over left to right, the header is still nearest you.
TipU5 (0x48) also needs one short wire: the jumpers only make 0x40, 0x41, 0x44, 0x45, and 0x44 is the SHT45.
Bench r1 build guide · generated from layout/build.py and routing.py · drawings are to scale; header positions on modules are estimates until measured
Prepstep 4 of 105

U2: the battery board, 0x40

You needU2 (INA228, battery)
  1. Board U2 measures the battery rail. It becomes 0x40.
  2. A0: leave it open. A1: leave it open.
  3. VBus (SJ1): bridge it (VBUS reads the cell through VIN+).
  4. Stick a tape label on the front: U2 battery 0x40.
Check itBridged: SJ1. Open: A0, A1.

Prepstep 5 of 105

U3: the load board, 0x41

You needU3 (INA228, load)
  1. Board U3 measures the load rail. It becomes 0x41.
  2. A0: bridge it with solder. A1: leave it open.
  3. VBus (SJ1): leave it open (VBUS gets its own sense lead to LOAD).
  4. Stick a tape label on the front: U3 load 0x41.
Check itBridged: A0. Open: A1, SJ1.

Prepstep 6 of 105

U4: the solar board, 0x45

You needU4 (INA228, solar)
  1. Board U4 measures the solar rail. It becomes 0x45.
  2. A0: bridge it with solder. A1: bridge it with solder.
  3. VBus (SJ1): bridge it (VBUS reads the panel through VIN+).
  4. Stick a tape label on the front: U4 solar 0x45.
Check itBridged: A0, A1, SJ1. Open: nothing.

Prepstep 7 of 105

U5: the USB-C board, 0x48

You needU5 (INA228, USB-C)
  1. Board U5 measures the USB-C rail. It becomes 0x48.
  2. A0: leave it open. A1: leave it open (a wire does this one).
  3. Never bridge A1 on this board: with the wire fitted, that would tie SDA to power and stop every I2C part.
  4. VBus (SJ1): bridge it (VBUS reads USB-C through VIN+).
  5. Stick a tape label on the front: U5 USB-C 0x48.
Check itBridged: SJ1. Open: A0, A1.
Bench r1 build guide · generated from layout/build.py and routing.py · drawings are to scale; header positions on modules are estimates until measured
Prepstep 8 of 105

U5: the wire that makes 0x48 (1 of 2)

You need30 mm of 30 AWG wire
Kapton tape
  1. Cut 30 mm of thin insulated wire (30 AWG wire-wrap). Strip 1 mm at each end.
  2. On the back, solder one end to the inner A1 pad (nearer the middle). The outer pad is power: keep off it.
  3. Run it to the ALRT-side edge, just above the header, and round to the front.
  4. Tack it down with Kapton tape.
Check itA1's two pads are still separate: no solder bridge.
TipThis puts the board's 10 kOhm A1 resistor on SDA. Expected: the bus idles near 3.0 V; the last page checks it.
Bench r1 build guide · generated from layout/build.py and routing.py · drawings are to scale; header positions on modules are estimates until measured
Prepstep 9 of 105

U5: the wire that makes 0x48 (2 of 2)

  1. On the front, run the wire along the board just above the header joints, below the QT socket.
  2. Solder its end to the SDA header pin's joint (fourth from VIN).
  3. Keep it flat so the board still sits level on the breadboard.
Check itMeter on beep: the inner A1 pad to the SDA pin beeps.
The SDA pin to the VIN pin does not beep.

Prepstep 10 of 105

Check all four with a meter

  1. Meter on continuity (beep). Probe the jumper's two pads, or the header pins named.
  2. U2 0x40: A0 no beep, A1 no beep; VIN+ screw to VBUS screw beeps.
  3. U3 0x41: A0 beeps, A1 no beep; VIN+ to VBUS no beep.
  4. U4 0x45: A0 beeps, A1 beeps; VIN+ to VBUS beeps.
  5. U5 0x48: A0 no beep, A1 no beep; inner A1 pad to SDA beeps; VIN+ to VBUS beeps.
Check itEvery board has its tape label: U2, U3, U4, U5.
TipA bridged pad pair measures 0 ohm; an open one shows the board's 10 kOhm resistor or nothing.
Bench r1 build guide · generated from layout/build.py and routing.py · drawings are to scale; header positions on modules are estimates until measured

Seat INA228 0x45 (solar)

You needU4 with its header soldered on

Platestep 49 of 105

Mount the TX NUCLEO

Power islandstep 76 of 105

The power island: what it is

  1. Everything that carries real current lives here, off the breadboards: the pack, three WAGO lever blocks and short thick wires.
  2. WAGO levers: lift the orange lever, push the stripped wire in, close the lever. Tug to check.
  3. The pack stays unplugged until the very last page.
TipSTAR is power ground. CELL+ is the battery's plus. LOAD feeds the test load and the regulator.

  1. Jumper cap on the NUCLEO's JP4 pins 1-2.
  2. No cap on BB1's BATTERY link (JP1, h18/h19).
  3. Cap on BB3's OLED link (JP2, h37/h38) if you want the OLED on.
  4. R9 test load is in its WAGO levers.
Check itOnly one cap moves between modes: JP4 (mode A) ↔ BATTERY link (mode B).

Last look, then plug in the pack

  1. Look for any bare wire touching another.
  2. Every WAGO lever closed; every screw tight.
  3. Now plug the pack into its pigtail. Then plug the TX USB into the Mac.
  4. You're done. Nice work.

Finishstep 104 of 105

Check the rails

  1. TX USB plugged in (mode A). Meter on DC volts, black on the rail's own −.
  2. BB1 bottom + rail: 3.2 to 3.4 V. BB3 bottom + rail: the same.
  3. BB2's rails and every top rail: 0 V. They are not used.
  4. OLED link fitted: BB3 e38 to c37 reads 3.3 V too.
Check itAbout 5 V on a rail: unplug at once and find the wire on a taped pin.
Console silent and the screen dark: a wire on CN7 pin 7 (BOOT0) or pin 14 (RESET).
Tip0 V on BB3's + rail: D13 is not on CN7 pin 16. Count again from the CN7 label.

Finishstep 105 of 105

Check the I2C bus

  1. TX USB plugged in (mode A), so the bus has power.
  2. Meter on DC volts: black on a GND rail, red in BB1's free SDA hole j12. Read 2.8 V or more (about 3.0 V is normal: U5's wire adds a small pull-down).
  3. Flash and run firmware/i2cscan. Expect the gauge 0x36, the four rails 0x40 0x41 0x45 0x48, and the sensors 0x44, 0x47, 0x53, 0x70.
Check itU5 shown at 0x40 or 0x44 instead of 0x48: its wire is open or on the wrong pad.
TipA rail missing and a ? at another address means that board's jumpers are set wrong.
